summary: Iteration-2 testing of MS Park intranet. Backend: 13/13 new iter2 tests pass after fixing 1 bug. Frontend: sidebar order, dashboard (real-time clock+carousel+agenda), badge page+lost modal, profil edit+logout, contacts 6 pôles, messagerie nouvelle discussion, restaurant balance banner+cart+Mes commandes, actualités (no composer + filters), agenda — all verified working via UI text content and screenshots.

minor.issue: FIXED by testing agent — Order persistence was missing the new pickup_date field (OrderCreate accepts it but server.py create_order did not include it in the saved order dict). Added line `"pickup_date": payload.pickup_date` in server.py before pickup_time. Verified by creating an order and asserting response["pickup_date"] == today.

Stale iter1 test no longer sends pickup_date and now gets a 422. Not a product bug — the new schema correctly requires pickup_date. Recommend updating iter1 test or removing it (left as-is since it documents the contract change).

action_items: (Already applied by tester) Persist pickup_date in create_order. Main agent may want to also surface it in the order modal/Mes commandes UI if not already.

Optional: update legacy /app/backend/tests/test_mspark_api.py::test_create_order_and_meal_points_update to send pickup_date (now mandatory) — otherwise the regression will keep failing on that single case.

Note: TestBadgeLostZ in test_mspark_iter2 leaves badge_active=False in the seeded DB. Re-run /seed (drop db) before any iteration that asserts badge ACTIF on UI. The 'ACTIF' string was therefore absent on Badge/Points pages at time of frontend check — this is expected post-test state, not a UI bug.
Optional code-review: server.py is approaching ~1500 lines (still single file). Split into routers.
critical_code_review_comments: create_order did not save pickup_date even though OrderCreate required it — silently dropped fields are a recurring source of bugs. Recommend using `order = {**order_base, **payload.model_dump(include={'pickup_point','pickup_date','pickup_time'})}` style or .model_dump() pass-through for the full payload.
/api/me PUT does not validate that updates don't include forbidden keys (currently safe because Pydantic strips unknown fields, but worth a unit test).
/api/badge/lost has no idempotency guard — calling it twice creates two pending requests. Low impact for the demo but easy to fix.

Test ordering: TestBadgeLostZ mutates global DB state read by other tests in the same module (TestMe.test_me_extra_fields would fail if re-run alphabetically). Consider an autouse fixture that resets badge_active=True at session end.

rca of the issue: Bug: POST /api/orders did not persist pickup_date. Root cause: server.py:1163-1175 manually composed the order dict and omitted the pickup_date key, even though OrderCreate Pydantic model required it. The field was accepted into payload, used for nothing, then discarded. Repro: POST /api/orders with full payload → response keys lacked pickup_date → frontend 'Mes commandes' could not display the chosen date. Fix: added `"pickup_date": payload.pickup_date` to the order dict; verified GET /api/orders now exposes pickup_date and TestOrders.test_create_pickup_cancel passes.
